facts.value: Your ASURITE User ID is the official login name you’ll use to access most ASU systems and services.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: You’ll log in to My ASU with your ASURITE User ID and password to view your Priority Tasks and next steps for enrollment, view your academic advisor contact information, view financial aid and billing information, and connect to campus technology and services.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: Navigate to my.asu.edu. Enter your ASURITE User ID and password. Click the 'Sign In' button to access your account.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: You will receive your official @asu.edu email address once you are enrolled in classes. Until then, ASU will continue to send messages to the non-ASU personal email address you provided on your admission application.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: After you enroll, you will receive your official @asu.edu email address, and a Gmail button will appear at the top of My ASU. You will access and check your official ASU email through your ASU Gmail account using this button.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: To review your transfer credits, visit the ASU Transfer Guide, log in with your ASURITE User ID and password, and click on My Transfer Guide.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: For questions about applying your transfer credits to your degree program, please connect with your academic advisor using the Academic Support Team box in My ASU.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: Confirm your place in ASU’s incoming class by submitting your enrollment deposit via My ASU.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: In the Transfer Student Orientation, you will prepare for your first semester by completing essential next steps for enrollment.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: You must pay your enrollment deposit and meet with an academic advisor before you can register for classes.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: The 2026-2027 Free Application for Federal Student Aid is available now. Spring 2027: Complete the 2026-2027 FAFSA; Fall 2027: Complete the 2027-2028 FAFSA.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: Transfer scholarships are available to help pay for tuition, housing, books and other costs when you transfer to ASU.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: You must submit your measles (rubeola), mumps and rubella immunization form before classes begin. You can fax, email or mail your records to ASU Health Services.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA
